title: sse: fix partial JSON delimiter & token/event ordering in streaming responses
author: Ravi Patel
description: Context: Several production incidents surfaced where SSE streaming payloads occasionally produced partial JSON objects or delivered token/event fragments out of order when the connection experienced bursts/packet coalescing. This caused downstream OpenAI-compatible clients and structured-output parsers to fail intermittently (ENG-1457). Motivation: Make streaming framing deterministic across TCP re-assembly and intermediary proxies, ensure delimiter tokens and partial-json boundaries are emitted in a stable order, and add defenses for client-side tolerant parsing. Changes: - Strengthen the chunking layer to ensure event delimiters ("data: " prefixes and double-newline separators) are always flushed before partial-json fragments are sent. - Add a small sequencing layer for tokens vs. control events so that control events (e.g., [DONE], tool-calls metadata) are ordered after their final token chunks. - Normalize newline handling: convert CRLF to LF at the emitter boundary to avoid proxy-induced double-newline anomalies. - Add unit & integration tests that simulate packet-splitting and TCP reassemble ordering. - Small compatibility tweaks in redwood-openai-compat to accept tolerant partial-json boundaries and retry incomplete parse attempts. Checklist: - [x] Repro script that simulates packet-split streaming - [x] Unit tests for framing logic - [x] Integration test against redwood-openai-compat harness - [x] Bench sanity check for throughput impact (<=1% overhead) - [x] Security review completed (no new surface) Notes: This is a targeted fix for streaming stability; it does not change the public API semantics. The additional sequencing buffer is bounded and should not impact latency materially. See linked Linear tickets for incident details.

review_conversation: Elena Garcia: Please add a microbenchmark that measures framing overhead. We saw 2-3% in prior attempts.

Connor Reed: Can you explain the sequencer bounds and what happens under extreme backlog? Add a safety drop or backpressure.

Ravi Patel: Sequencer is bounded to 512 entries and enqueues only control events (which are low-volume). On overflow we drop non-essential metadata and emit an explicit warning event; added tests for this path.
Priya Nair: openai-compat changes look good. Please ensure we don't silently swallow parse errors — added a small change request.
Ravi Patel: Updated parser to surface a non-fatal parse-warning event and retry up to 2 times before failing the stream. Tests added.

release_notes: Fix streaming SSE framing which could emit partial JSON fragments or out-of-order control events causing client parse failures. No API changes. Improved robustness for OpenAI-compatible streaming clients.
